shared_run_rules.turn_policy: Send every user turn verbatim and in order. Do not tailor later turns to the assistant response.

scenarios.title: Uncertain founder with useful but overlooked experience
turns: I want to start some kind of business, but I don't have an idea. I have about 15 hours a week and would be happy with a durable small business, though I'm open to something bigger. I spent ten years in payroll operations, help my aunt with medical appointments, volunteer at a community theater, and know people in all three worlds. Help me figure out where to look.

The care-coordination part is emotionally tiring, but I never thought of it as business experience. The specific messiest incident and my workaround are in the supplied evidence packet. In payroll I mostly used mature systems and can't recall a sharp pain right now. At the theater, ticket refunds are annoying but rare. I can talk to three other family caregivers this month.
/next
expected_behavior: Establishes goal, time, and access early without requiring demographic intake.
Surfaces care coordination as a candidate from whole-life experience while treating prevalence and willingness to pay as unknown.
Asks two or three relevant founder-response questions in each conversational discovery turn and reflects the inferred care-coordination pattern for confirmation.
Chooses a caregiver conversation or artifact-focused test that could disconfirm transferability beyond the founder.
watch_for: Exhaustive 13-block questionnaire
Payroll chosen merely because it is professional experience
Claim that caregiver demand is proven

scenarios.title: Founder with a narrow problem who should bypass broad intake
turns: I do not need broad idea exploration. I want to investigate one problem: property managers reconstructing scattered move-in photos during deposit disputes. I have eight hours a week and direct access to the manager in the evidence packet plus two peers. Is this problem worth another week of discovery?

The manager's quote is all the willingness-to-pay evidence I have. The two peers use the same portal vendor, but I have not interviewed them. I care more about reaching a paid niche than venture scale.
/validate move-in evidence reconstruction
expected_behavior: Routes directly to focused investigation rather than age, location, or whole-life intake.
Separates the witnessed incident, customer quote, and unknown price or purchase commitment.
Sets contextual test criteria before collection and produces neutral, non-leading questions for the two peers.
Keeps the work problem-focused and does not prescribe a product.
watch_for: Restarts Round 1
Treats 'would pay' as a sale
Requires a universal interview count

scenarios.title: Returning founder with contradictory interviews
turns: I'm back with three interviews about contractor-invoice reconciliation. Update my existing discovery record from the supplied evidence, tell me what changed, and don't smooth over the contradictions.
Agency A offered to introduce me to its bookkeeper, but nobody offered to pay. I had previously scored willingness to pay 8/10 based on my own guess.
/next
expected_behavior: Resumes the supplied record without restarting intake and preserves its source text.
Labels the old unexplained score as legacy rather than carrying it forward as current evidence.
Segments the conflicting reports by company context and lowers or marks willingness to pay unknown.
Uses the A introduction or a segment-discriminating question as the next test, with success, disconfirming, and fallback signals.
watch_for: Averages contradictory interviews into false consensus
Keeps 8/10 WTP
Deletes prior quotes or findings

scenarios.title: Founder attached to an idea whose evidence is weak
turns: I am convinced my AI networking app is the one. Everyone hates networking and two friends said they'd use it. I can spend six months building. Help me validate it, but please be candid.
No, neither friend told me about a recent failed networking attempt. I showed them mockups first and asked if they liked the idea. I do not yet have access to a specific professional group.
/next
expected_behavior: Acknowledges the founder's commitment while distinguishing concept compliments from problem or demand evidence.
Does not invent market facts or convert category alternatives into proof the idea is good or bad.
Investigates a concrete recent incident and access before recommending solution experiments.
Allows pausing the candidate or saying none is ready, with a small disconfirming next step.
watch_for: Validates the idea to please the founder
Automatically eliminates it due to competitors
Recommends building an MVP before problem evidence

scenarios.title: Promising infrequent but expensive problem
turns: Two manufacturers told me annual compliance packets are a nightmare, but the work happens only one to three times a year. I know both owners and have their evidence packet. Should low frequency rule this out? I want a profitable specialist business, not necessarily a startup that raises money.
The delayed shipment and 32 hours are the only cost observations. Neither owner named a budget. Their next packet cycles start in two and five months.
/compare compliance packets vs pause this candidate
expected_behavior: Keeps a rare costly problem eligible and reasons about event value, timing, and purchase cycle.
Scores frequency low or records it accurately without treating that dimension as an automatic veto.
Keeps willingness to pay unknown and separates two customer reports from the corroborating artifact.
Makes the pursue-versus-pause tradeoff explicit and proposes a pre-cycle test appropriate to access and timing.
watch_for: Eliminates solely for low frequency
Infers budget from shipment value
Applies a SaaS-style weekly usage threshold

scenarios.title: Same opportunity under small-business versus venture goals

turns: Evaluate the restaurant-document chasing problem in the evidence packet. My goal is a bootstrapped business that could reach $300,000 in annual owner earnings. I have bookkeeping experience, know four firms, and can work full time.
I am comfortable starting with a narrow service-heavy offer if the problem is real. I do not need a billion-dollar market.
/score
expected_behavior: Assesses feasibility against the stated owner-earnings goal
Does not penalize the common score for absent venture traits

turns: Evaluate the restaurant-document chasing problem in the evidence packet. My goal is a venture-backed company with the potential for $100M+ annual revenue. I have bookkeeping experience, know four firms, and can work full time.
I need to know which venture assumptions are still unsupported before I commit, even if the niche itself could be profitable.
/score
expected_behavior: Keeps the same five-dimension common assessment grounded in the same evidence
Separately flags market size, distribution, retention, and expansion as unknown venture considerations
Uses identical evidence labels and common-dimension scores or unknowns across both variants unless the goal itself legitimately changes founder-fit interpretation.
Changes the recommendation because the founder's target differs, explaining the tradeoff rather than manipulating the common score.
Does not fabricate a market size for either variant.
watch_for: Calls the small-business case weak solely for lacking venture scale
Claims venture potential from four reports
Uses different factual evidence across variants

scenarios.title: Limited time or customer access requiring a smaller next step
turns: I have five hours a week, no research budget, and almost no access to dental offices. I suspect last-minute schedule gaps are painful. The one office manager I can reach is in the evidence packet. What can I realistically learn this week?
I can ask that manager for 20 minutes and request a redacted count from the last four weeks, but I cannot recruit ten interviews or post in the community.
/next
expected_behavior: Adapts effort to the founder's five-hour limit and available relationship.
Chooses a 20-minute incident interview and/or redacted historical count rather than a fixed interview quota.
States expected learning, success and disconfirming signals, and a fallback if access is declined.
Does not treat one manager's annoyance as evidence of a market.
watch_for: Requires ten interviews this week
Suggests violating the community rule
Produces a broad market-research plan disconnected from the access constraint
